fields.System.Title: FDN-5 — Master data: locations
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Define the physical shape of the warehouse: sites, zones, and the exact positions stock can sit
in — including the virtual ones that make the ledger balance.

Scope

In. Warehouses, zones, locations with capacity and sequence, bulk import, blocking,
retirement, virtual locations.

Out. Slotting — deciding which product belongs in which location. Warehouse layout CAD.

Design notes

Structured location codes. PICK-A-12-03 — zone, aisle, bay, level. Pick sequencing,
replenishment source-finding, and reporting all depend on being able to reason about a code. An
opaque UUID on a label makes every one of those harder.

pick_sequence is quietly critical. Two adjacent locations must have adjacent sequence
numbers or pickers walk the aisle twice. It is invisible in testing — every test passes — and
expensive every day in production. Leave gaps (10, 20, 30) so new locations can be inserted.

Capacity is not optional. If putaway needs weight and volume limits, make them required at
creation. Null is not a capacity, and a null makes the algorithm suggest nonsense.

Virtual locations are a small idea with a large payoff. VIRT-SUPPLIER, VIRT-CUSTOMER,
VIRT-LOSS, VIRT-GAIN, VIRT-INTRANSIT. With them, every movement is a transfer between two
locations and total quantity is conserved — which is what makes the ledger reconcile.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Null capacity breaks putaway suggestions | [doc 03 §7.4](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Wrong pick sequence costs hours of walking daily | [doc 03 §4](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Retiring a location that still holds stock | [doc 03 §5](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Blocking a location with open tasks against it | [doc 03 §7.7](../../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Partial bulk import | [doc 09 §11.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
